title: Supported etale generators for cohomological support filtrations
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the unbounded ordinary small etale derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $(\Phi^a)_{a\in\mathbf Z}$ be subsets of $|X|$, each stable under specialization, with $\Phi^{a+1}\subseteq\Phi^a$ and $\Phi^a=|X|$ for every $a\leq b$, for some integer $b$. For a sheaf $F$, its support is the set of points with nonzero geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Choose a small skeleton of affine etale $X$-schemes $u:V\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For each closed reduced subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $u(|Z|)\subseteq\Phi^a$, put $G_{V,Z,a}=u_!i_*\Lambda_Z[-a]$. Here $\Lambda_Z$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $i_*$ is closed direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $u_!$ is the exact left adjoint to etale restriction, equivalently the sheafified sum over lifts to $V$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. The full subcategory
$$\mathcal U_\Phi=\{K:\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^a(K)\subseteq\Phi^a\text{ for every }a\}$$
is the smallest strictly full subcategory containing all $G_{V,Z,a}$ and zero and closed under small coproducts, direct summands, $[1]$, and extensions. No constructibility or finite-dimensionality hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: XVII 5.2, support half of Gabber's construction: agent-formulated supported-generator input. The unrestricted generators are stated in lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian; the additional filtered-support assertion is a separate obligation. Full Gabber proof source WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C$ for the closure of the stated generators under the five operations. The module-sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] computes its derived coproducts termwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], geometric stalks of module sheaves are exact and commute with small coproducts: apply the latter two statements after forgetting the module structure, using the first statement. Consequently $H^q(\bigoplus K_t)_{\bar x}=\bigoplus H^q(K_t)_{\bar x}$, by computing kernels and images of the termwise sum of complexes. Thus $\mathcal U_\Phi$ is closed under coproducts and summands. It is closed under extensions by the long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], tested at these exact stalks. It is closed under $[1]$ since $H^q(K[1])=H^{q+1}(K)$ and $\Phi^{q+1}\subseteq\Phi^q$.

source.place: Tags 03DB (module colimits), 03PT (exact stalks), 07D9 (derived coproducts); derived long exact sequence

proof.text: For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$, [lem-kun-04ca] says that $i_*\Lambda_Z$ has zero geometric stalk off $Z$. These stalk assertions for underlying abelian sheaves retain their module meaning because forgetting modules is exact and faithful [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. By the direct-sum formula [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks], $u_!i_*\Lambda_Z$ has zero geometric stalk outside $u(|Z|)$. Hence each $G_{V,Z,a}$ has cohomology only in degree $a$, supported in $\Phi^a$. Zero also satisfies the support condition. Step 1 and minimality give $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal U_\Phi$.

Both the definition of a telescope [def-kun-truncations] and [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] apply to module sheaves on the small etale site without boundedness. If $E_n\in\mathcal C$, rotate its telescope triangle to $\bigoplus E_n\to\operatorname{hocolim} E_n\to(\bigoplus E_n)[1]$. Both end objects are in $\mathcal C$, so its middle object is too. In particular, for a sequence of actual complexes in $\mathcal C$, its termwise colimit belongs to $\mathcal C$ by that lemma. We shall use this only for explicit increasing truncation subcomplexes.

source.place: Derived Categories, Tag 0949 (lemma-colim-hocolim), and telescope definition

proof.text: Fix a sheaf $F$ with support in a subset $S\subseteq|X|$, an affine etale object $u:V\to X$ in the chosen skeleton, and $s\in F(V)$. Apply [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open] to the underlying abelian sheaf. Its zero open $W\subseteq V$ has closed complement $T$, and $u(T)\subseteq S$: a point outside $S$ has zero stalk, hence every germ of $s$ there is zero and the point lies in $W$. Give $T$ its reduced closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The section $s$ defines the linear map $\Lambda_V\to F|_V$, $1\mapsto s$, by sheafifying the constant-presheaf map. Its restriction to $W$ is zero. The module version of [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], applied to $\Lambda_V$, and [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] identify its quotient by $j_!\Lambda_W$ with $i_*\Lambda_Z$. The cokernel property therefore factors the map through $i_*\Lambda_Z\to F|_V$.

Transpose the map of Step 4 along the module adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] to obtain $u_!i_*\Lambda_Z\to F$. Take the coproduct of these maps over all pairs $(V,s)$. This is a set: the affine etale skeleton is small and each $F(V)$ is a set. It is an epimorphism. Indeed every element of every geometric stalk of $F$ is represented by some such $s$, after passing to an affine neighbourhood and a skeleton representative, by [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The quotient $\Lambda_V\to i_*\Lambda_Z$ followed by the factor map is the original map $1\mapsto s$; the adjunction's section map sends its germ back to that same germ of $s$. This also follows directly from the summand/germ formula of [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks]. The cokernel therefore has zero stalks by exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and is zero by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Forgetting modules is exact and faithful [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so this is an epimorphism of module sheaves as well.

Now take $S=\Phi^a$ and $\operatorname{Supp}F\subseteq S$. Steps 2 and 5 give an epimorphism $P_0\to F$ where $P_0$ is a coproduct of $u_!i_*\Lambda_Z$ supported in $S$. Its kernel is supported in $S$ by exactness of geometric stalks (and the exact module forgetful functor) [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Repeat Step 5 on that kernel, and then recursively on each next kernel. This constructs an exact augmented resolution $\cdots\to P_2\to P_1\to P_0\to F\to0$, all $P_n$ coproducts of supported generators without shifts. Place $P_n$ in degree $a-n$; the resulting bounded-above complex $P$ maps quasi-isomorphically to $F[-a]$, since the displayed resolution is exact. Each term as a single-degree object belongs to $\mathcal C$: $P_n[-a][n]$ is a coproduct of the prescribed generators at index $a$, shifted by the nonnegative integer $n$.

source.place: Tags 03PT, 03DI, 03EW; iterative kernels of the supported epimorphisms of Steps 4--5

proof.text: For the resolution $P$ of Step 6 take its finite brutal subcomplexes $\sigma_{\ge a-n}P$. Each is a finite iterated extension of its terms placed in their degrees: remove its lowest degree to get a short exact sequence whose subcomplex is the higher-degree tail and whose quotient is that lowest term. [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] turns this sequence into the requisite extension triangle. By induction from the zero complex and Step 6 these finite complexes belong to $\mathcal C$. Their inclusions have termwise colimit $P$, so Step 3 proves $F[-a]\in\mathcal C$. More generally, the identical finite-tail argument shows that any bounded-above complex whose individual degree terms lie in $\mathcal C$ belongs to $\mathcal C$; it uses no projectivity or lifting of maps.

For every $q\le b$ the equality $\Phi^q=X$ lets Step 7 apply to every sheaf $F$, giving $F[-q]\in\mathcal C$. If $K\in D^{\mathrm{ord},\le b}$, the representative criterion of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] gives a complex zero in degrees above $b$. All its degree terms, placed in their degrees, are therefore in $\mathcal C$. The finite-tail argument of Step 7 and Step 3 put $K$ in $\mathcal C$. This establishes the uniform starting class $D^{\mathrm{ord},\le b}\subseteq\mathcal C$, even for complexes unbounded below.

source.place: Standard truncation representative and Tag 0949, starting bound $b$

proof.text: Let $K\in\mathcal U_\Phi$. Step 8 puts $\tau_{\le b}K$ in $\mathcal C$. Induct on $n\ge b$: the triangle [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] has end objects $\tau_{\le n-1}K$ and $H^n(K)[-n]$. The former is in $\mathcal C$ by induction; the latter is in $\mathcal C$ by Step 7 because $\operatorname{Supp}H^n(K)\subseteq\Phi^n$. Thus $\tau_{\le n}K\in\mathcal C$ for every $n\ge b$. For an actual representative of $K$, these good truncation subcomplexes form a sequence with termwise colimit that representative: in each degree $q$ the terms and differential are unchanged once $n>q$. Apply [lem-kun-complex-colimit-hocolim] and Step 3 to conclude $K\in\mathcal C$. Together with Step 2 this proves the equality. The zero scheme and the zero coefficient ring yield zero objects throughout, with the same argument.

source.place: Derived Categories, Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle) and Tag 0949 (colimit telescope)
